Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("(MM) with μ_i + μ'_i, G := W_k, (a, b) := (−m, m) gives, for a.e. t, liminf_i(M_{W_k}(Z_{i,t}) + M_{W_k}(∂B_{i,t})) < ∞ for all k"), written for arbitrary measures μ_i and majorized functions Z_{i,k}. Put Λ_k := sup_i μ_i(W_k) < ∞.

Its finiteness hypothesis is the bound just proved, and its majorant hypothesis is the assumed inequality for Z_{j,k}(t), used only for t ∈ (−m, m). (MM) yields a measurable g = g_{k,m} : ℝ → [0, ∞] with (α) for L¹-a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t); and (β) ∫_{(−m,m)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(E).

So ∫ g d(L¹ restricted to (−m, m)) ≠ ∞, and since g is measurable, g(t) < ∞ for (L¹ restricted to (−m, m))-a.e. t (Mathlib ae_lt_top). As (−m, m) is measurable (measurableSet_Ioo), this means (ae_restrict_iff'): for L¹-a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies g(t) < ∞.
3. Intersecting the two full-measure sets of (α) and step 2: for L¹-a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t) < ∞.
4. Still for fixed k: a countable intersection of full-measure sets has full measure (ae_all_iff over m ∈ ℕ), so for L¹-a.e. t, for every m ∈ ℕ, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. For such t choose m ∈ ℕ with m > |t| (exists_nat_gt); then −m < t < m (neg_abs_le, le_abs_self), so liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. Thus for each k, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t.
5. Applying ae_all_iff once more, over k ∈ ℕ, gives: for L¹-a.e. t, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ. ∎

subproblem.title: Level sets of a measure finite on compact sets are null at almost every level (parent step 4, countable_meas_level_set_pos)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ν be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra of Euclid P) with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be measurable. Then ν({x : f(x) = t}) = 0 for L¹-almost every t ∈ ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), Measurable f → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ν {x | f x = t} = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("ν{f = t} = ν'{f = t} = 0 off a countable set (countable_meas_level_set_pos)"), stated for one measure ν. Write E_t := {x : f(x) = t}.
1. ν is s-finite. By hypothesis ν is finite on every compact set (Mathlib class IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts, built from the hypothesis as ⟨fun K hK => h K hK⟩). ℝ^P is locally compact, so every point has a compact neighbourhood (a closed ball) of finite ν-measure, i.e. ν is locally finite (Mathlib instance isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). A locally finite measure on a second-countable space is σ-finite (Mathlib instance sigmaFinite_of_locallyFinite; ℝ^P is second countable), hence s-finite.
2. Countably many charged levels. The sets E_t (t ∈ ℝ) are measurable (f is measurable and singletons of ℝ are measurable) and pairwise disjoint. For an s-finite measure and measurable f, the set S := {t ∈ ℝ : 0 < ν(E_t)} is countable (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos). For completeness: write ν = Σ_n ν_n with finite ν_n; if ν(E_t) > 0 then ν_n(E_t) > 1/m for some n, m ∈ ℕ; for fixed n, m at most m·ν_n(ℝ^P) of the disjoint sets E_t satisfy ν_n(E_t) > 1/m; so S is a countable union of finite sets.
3. A countable subset of ℝ is Lebesgue-null (it is a countable union of null singletons; Set.Countable.measure_zero). Hence L¹(S) = 0.
4. In [0, ∞], ν(E_t) ≠ 0 if and only if 0 < ν(E_t) (pos_iff_ne_zero). Therefore L¹({t : ¬ ν(E_t) = 0}) = L¹(S) = 0, which is exactly the statement that ν(E_t) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t (Mathlib ae_iff). ∎
proof_key_steps: ν is finite on compact sets, hence locally finite and σ-finite (s-finite) on ℝ^P.
Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos: only countably many of the disjoint level sets {f = t} have positive ν-measure.
Countable subsets of ℝ are Lebesgue-null, so ν{f = t} = 0 for a.e. t (ae_iff).

audit.reason: Prose and type agree. Compact finiteness supplies sigma-finiteness; measurability gives countably many charged levels, whose Lebesgue measure is zero. The proof establishes the exact almost-everywhere conclusion without additional assumptions.

CL_P(d) is applied in the open ball B_1(x) ⊆ W_k (an open subset of ℝ^P, as CL_P(d) allows) instead of in W_k followed by a further restriction to B_1(x); this uses the same bounds and avoids composing domain restrictions. Notation: for V ⊆ U and S ∈ 𝒟_n(U), S|_V := S.restrictDomain ∈ 𝒟_n(V), S|_V(ω) = S(ω~), where ω~ := testFormOnInclusion(ω) ∈ 𝒟^n(U) has the same underlying form as ω. Put u_{i,k} := M_{W_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, W_k) ∈ [0, ∞]; by hypothesis liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞ for every k.
1. Restriction facts, for a fresh degree m (prove them by cases on m, not on d), V ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and sets W ⊆ W'. (a) M_W(S|_V) ≤ M_{W'}(S): M_W(S|_V) is the supremum of ofReal(S|_V(ω)) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^m(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn); for such ω, ω~ has the same underlying form, so it is admissible for M_{W'}(S) (tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ W'), and ofReal(S|_V(ω)) = ofReal(S(ω~)) ≤ M_{W'}(S) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn); conclude with sSup_le. (b) boundaryMassOn(S|_V, W) ≤ boundaryMassOn(S, W'): if m = 0 both sides are 0; if m = e + 1, (S|_V).boundary = (S.boundary)|_V, because both send η ∈ 𝒟^e(V) to S evaluated at a test form whose underlying form is dη (GeometricCurrentOn.ext; the two values agree definitionally), so the claim is (a) applied to S.boundary.
2. Z has locally finite mass. Let W be open with closure(W) compact. A compact set is bounded, so closure(W) ⊆ B_r(0) for some r (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball); choose k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ r (exists_nat_ge); then W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ B_r(0) ⊆ W_k. By monotonicity of mass in the region (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono), lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) and M ≤ M + boundaryMassOn (liminf_le_liminf with le_self_add): M_W(Z) ≤ M_{W_k}(Z) ≤ liminf_i M_{W_k}(Z_i) ≤ liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞.
3. Z|_{B_1(x)} is IM for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Choose k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ |x|; then B_1(x) ⊆ W_k, since |y − x| < 1 gives |y| ≤ |y − x| + |x| < 1 + k (ball_subset_ball' with dist(x, 0) = |x|). Since liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞, choose C with liminf_i u_{i,k} < C < ∞ (exists_between). Then u_{i,k} < C for frequently many i in atTop (Filter.frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt; its coboundedness side condition holds automatically in [0, ∞]), so there is a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with u_{ψ(l),k} ≤ C for all l (Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop). Put Y_l := Z_{ψ(l)}|_{B_1(x)} and Y := Z|_{B_1(x)} in 𝒟_d(B_1(x)).
(i) Every Y_l is IM, by IML_P(d)(2) with U := ℝ^P (open), V := B_1(x) (open) and X := Z_{ψ(l)}.
(ii) Y_l ⇀ Y in B_1(x): for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(B_1(x)), Y_l(ω) = Z_{ψ(l)}(ω~) → Z(ω~) = Y(ω), since (Z_{ψ(l)}(ω~))_l is a subsequence of the convergent sequence (Z_i(ω~))_i (ψ is strictly increasing, so ψ(l) → ∞).
(iii) Let W'' be open with closure(W'') compact and contained in B_1(x). Then W'' ⊆ closure(W'') ⊆ B_1(x) ⊆ W_k, so by 1(a) and 1(b), for every l, M_{W''}(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W'') ≤ M_{W_k}(Z_{ψ(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{ψ(l)}, W_k) = u_{ψ(l),k} ≤ C. Hence sup_l (M_{W''}(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W'')) ≤ C < ∞ (iSup_le).
By CL_P(d) applied with U := B_1(x) (open), T_l := Y_l and T := Y, the current Z|_{B_1(x)} is IM.
4. Conclusion. By step 2 and step 3 (with r := 1 > 0 and B_1(x) ⊆ ℝ^P at every x ∈ ℝ^P), IML_P(d)(1) applied with U := ℝ^P (open) and X := Z shows that Z is IM. ∎

Lower semicontinuity: M_W(Z) ≤ liminf_i (M_{W_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, W_k)) < ∞ for W ⊆ W_k, so Z has locally finite mass.

For x ∈ ℝ^P take k ≥ |x| and a subsequence ψ with M_{W_k}(Z_{ψ(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{ψ(l)}, W_k) ≤ C; the IM restrictions Z_{ψ(l)}|_{B_1(x)} converge weakly to Z|_{B_1(x)} with bounded mass and boundary mass, so CL_P(d) on B_1(x) gives Z|_{B_1(x)} IM.
IML_P(d)(1) glues the local statements: Z is IM.

Source: parent step 5 ("(T2) for X_i ⇀ X and ∂X_i ⇀ ∂X gives A_{i,t}(ω) → A(ω) and B_{i,t}(η) → B(η), so Z_{i,t} ⇀ Z := ∂A − B").
1. Slices of X_j. Apply (T2) with k := d + 1, the open U, the sequence X_j ⇀ X, the representations (μ_j, ξ_j) of X_j and (μ_X, ξ_X) := (μ, ξ) of X, the measure ν in the role of the limit measure, the continuous f and the level t. Its hypotheses are hypotheses of the statement: μ_j(K) < ∞ and μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, a.e. strong measurability and the a.e. bounds of ξ_j and ξ, the representation identities of X_j and X, ν(K) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ ν(K) for compact K ⊆ U, and ν{f = t} = 0. It gives ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U); by the identities for A_j and A this is A_j(ω) → A(ω) (rewrite the limit by the identity for A and use Tendsto.congr with the identities for A_j).
2. Boundaries converge. For η ∈ 𝒟^d(U), dη ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U) and ∂X_j(η) = X_j(dη) → X(dη) = ∂X(η) (definition of the boundary, GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply; weak convergence tested on dη). So ∂X_j ⇀ ∂X in 𝒟_d(U).
3. Slices of ∂X_j. Apply (T2) with k := d, U, the sequence ∂X_j ⇀ ∂X of step 2, the representations (μ'_j, ξ'_j) of ∂X_j and (μ', ξ') of ∂X, the limit measure ν', f and t (again all hypotheses are given, including limsup_j μ'_j(K) ≤ ν'(K) and ν'{f = t} = 0). It gives ∫_{f<t}ξ'_j(η)dμ'_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', i.e. B_j(η) → B(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^d(U).
4. Conclusion. Subtraction of currents is pointwise and ∂S(η) = S(dη), so for η ∈ 𝒟^d(U), (∂A_j − B_j)(η) = A_j(dη) − B_j(η). By step 1 with ω := dη, step 3 and Tendsto.sub, this converges to A(dη) − B(η) = (∂A − B)(η). Hence ∂A_j − B_j ⇀ ∂A − B in 𝒟_d(U). ∎

(T2) in degree d for ∂X_j ⇀ ∂X with limit measure ν' gives B_j(η) → B(η).
(∂A_j − B_j)(η) = A_j(dη) − B_j(η) → A(dη) − B(η) = (∂A − B)(η).

subproblem.statement: Assume (SL), the type of the selected node's accepted dependency slicing (cmc_slice_mass_bounds), verbatim the first hypothesis: for all P, k ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T in U (measures on ℝ^P finite on compact subsets of U; a.e. strongly measurable fields of (k+1)- resp. k-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ'-a.e. x, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α; T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms in U) and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, there are A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η misses {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open W and all t, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ L · μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), (μ, ξ) an admissible representation of X and (μ', ξ') an admissible representation of ∂X in U (as above), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0). Then there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all t and all test forms ω, η in U, such that for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P and every t ∈ ℝ, with Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)(μ + μ')(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) in [0, ∞], where boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = M_W(∂Z_t) if d ≥ 1 and = 0 if d = 0.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 3 ((SL) for X_i and, if d ≥ 1, (SL) for ∂X_i with the representation (0, 0) of ∂∂X_i = 0), the identity ∂Z_{i,t} = −∂B_{i,t} of step 6 and the summed majorant (μ_i + μ'_i) of step 4, for one current X. Uses the accepted siblings boundary_slice (dmcbr_sl_sb_boundaryMassOn_slice_le), mass_neg (dmcbr_sl_sb_massOn_eq_of_apply_eq_neg) and liminf_add (dmcbr_sl_sb_ennreal_liminf_add_le). Notation: for an open W, t ∈ ℝ and a measure ν on ℝ^P, S_h := W ∩ {t − h < f < t} and ℓ_ν := liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)ν(S_h) (liminf along 𝓝[>]0, in [0, ∞]).
1. First slicing. Apply (SL) with k := d, the open U, T := X, the representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ', ξ') of ∂X, f and L; all its hypotheses are hypotheses of the statement. It yields families A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all t, ω, η; these are the required families. It also gives (i) M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·ℓ_μ for every open W and every t. Fix an open W and t ∈ ℝ and put Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t; it remains to prove the combined bound.
2. boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = boundaryMassOn(B_t, W). Prove, for a fresh degree m (case split on m, not on d), that boundaryMassOn(∂A' − B', W) = boundaryMassOn(B', W) for all A' ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) and B' ∈ 𝒟_m(U). If m = 0 both sides are 0 by the definition of boundaryMassOn. If m = e + 1, let ζ ∈ 𝒟^e(U). Subtraction of currents is pointwise and ∂T(ζ) = T(dζ) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), so ∂(∂A' − B')(ζ) = (∂A' − B')(dζ) = ∂A'(dζ) − B'(dζ) = ∂∂A'(ζ) − ∂B'(ζ). Since ∂∂A' = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary), this equals −∂B'(ζ). Hence mass_neg (with n := e, T₁ := ∂(∂A' − B'), T₂ := ∂B') gives M_W(∂(∂A' − B')) = M_W(∂B'), which is the claim for m = e + 1. Apply it with m := d, A' := A_t, B' := B_t.
3. Boundary bound. Apply boundary_slice with (SL), m := d, the open U, T := X, the representation (μ', ξ') of ∂X (finite on compacts of U, a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded, ∂X(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ'), f, L, t, B := B_t (whose values are ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' by step 1) and the open W. It gives boundaryMassOn(B_t, W) ≤ L·ℓ_{μ'}, so by step 2 boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L·ℓ_{μ'}.
4. Summation. For every h, ofReal(h⁻¹)·(μ + μ')(S_h) = ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(S_h) + ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ'(S_h) (Measure.add_apply and mul_add). By liminf_add with ι := ℝ and F := 𝓝[>]0, ℓ_μ + ℓ_{μ'} ≤ ℓ_{μ+μ'}.
5. Conclusion. By (i), step 3, distributivity and step 4 (multiplication by L in [0, ∞] is monotone): M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L·ℓ_μ + L·ℓ_{μ'} = L·(ℓ_μ + ℓ_{μ'}) ≤ L·ℓ_{μ+μ'}. ∎
proof_key_steps: (SL) for X with (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') gives A_t, B_t with the integral identities and M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·ℓ_μ.
For a fresh degree m, ∂(∂A' − B') = −∂B' pointwise (∂∂ = 0), so boundaryMassOn(∂A' − B', W) = boundaryMassOn(B', W) by mass_neg (both 0 if m = 0).
boundary_slice ((SL) for ∂X with the zero representation of ∂∂X) gives boundaryMassOn(B_t, W) ≤ L·ℓ_{μ'}.
(μ + μ')(S_h) splits termwise and liminf_add gives L·ℓ_μ + L·ℓ_{μ'} ≤ L·ℓ_{μ+μ'}.

audit.reason: All representation and slicing hypotheses are present. The proof correctly handles degree zero, identifies slice boundary mass using boundary squared zero and mass_neg, applies boundary_slice, and combines the bounds with the correctly directed ENNReal liminf inequality. Its three dependency edges are necessary and acyclic.
